# Frozen source restrictions

Assess Trent Horn and Raphael Lataster’s two openings, two rebuttal rounds, cross-examination and both closing statements only, approximately 4:06–1:10:46 and 1:40:19–1:48:30. Exclude every enumerated introduction, moderator-logistics, audience-Q&A and outro interval. Neither side receives credit, penalty, alleged concession or failure-to-reply inference from excluded material. Closing statements remain eligible as spoken, but their references to Q&A do not import omitted arguments or answers.

The frozen motion is Does God exist? Both speakers specify classical theism: Horn argues for necessary unlimited being with intellect, will and perfect goodness; Lataster challenges that specified God and the inference from generic supernaturalism. Lataster calls himself an agnostic non-theist and de facto naturalist. Do not assign him an unadopted burden of proving that no conceivable god exists; assess positive probability claims he actually makes.

Lataster grants supernaturalism and then monotheism for argument’s sake to focus on rival god concepts, expressly reiterating in his closing that he does not accept supernaturalism in reality. Horn’s contrary concession characterizations are Horn’s claims, not the source’s settled description. Preserve Lataster’s distinct arguments concerning polytheism, alternative monotheisms, deism/quasi-deism and pantheism/pandeism.

Horn offers contingency, a finite beginning, fine-tuning and objective moral facts as distinct lines, then argues they jointly lead to one unlimited perfectly good reality. Preserve his distinctions between a definition and an existence argument, mathematical or qualitative infinity and a temporal collection, moral ontology and how moral facts are known, and merely counting entities versus explanatory simplicity. None of these distinctions is automatically accepted or dismissed.

Lataster presents suffering and hiddenness as probabilistic evidence, not logical disproof. He distinguishes knowledge that God exists from choosing to follow God and argues that auxiliary excuses alter priors as well as likelihoods. Preserve Horn’s proposed reasons for hiddenness, including freedom, sharing belief and nonautomatic damnation. Neither side’s claim that the other gave no argument substitutes for examining the actual retained exchange.

Lataster’s demand for uncontroversial premises and sometimes 100% certainty is preserved alongside his uncertainty-based critique. Horn allows premises more likely true than false. Preserve their dispute over deductive validity, warrant for premises and probabilistic comparison without rewriting either position into a stronger one.

Cross-examination includes interruptions and mixed captions. At approximately 58:44–59:09 Lataster qualifies the limb-regrowth example: it might not establish God but could make a powerful figure worth following. At 59:59–1:00:18 he distinguishes eternalist theories from the B theory alone and says popularity does not prove truth. Preserve those qualifications. Moderator microphone directions and turn control are logistics only.

Automatic captions confuse names and technical terms, notably theism/deism/quasi-deism, pantheism, creatio ex nihilo, Borde–Guth–Vilenkin, Mackie and philosopher names. Numbers, quotations, scholarship claims and survey proportions remain speaker-reported evidence, not independently verified facts. Do not penalize recognition noise, silently repair an exact quotation or attribute an entire mixed turn to one speaker. Mark materially uncertain selected wording or speaker ownership below high confidence for targeted audio verification.

Five auxiliary source-audio transcriptions verify opening definitions/burdens, two round transitions and Lataster’s closing terminology and conditional grants. They do not replace canonical captions. The closing still contains self-correction about limited/unlimited concepts; do not build a penalty on that corrupted/self-corrected wording. Use stable completed claims, including the explicit conditional ontological-to-pantheistic inference. No direct listening is claimed.

All timed gaps longer than five seconds occur before speech, at applause/round transitions or in excluded Q&A; the two potentially ambiguous retained transitions were checked by auxiliary audio transcription and contain no missing substantive argument. Both complete closings are present. The moderator does not advance an independent motion argument in the retained scope.

Featured quotations must be exact complete 3–18 word thoughts, with clear referents and any necessary qualification or challenge preserved. Choose a different complete excerpt rather than completing, correcting or truncating source wording.
